Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

The trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

candidate.answer:
PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍连接）、纤维切断变短和细小纤维生成。 [2]
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
由WRV表征的润胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
PFI提高了片材拉伸强度，而zero-span拉伸指数表明PFI未降低纤维本身强度。 [1]
分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少以及结晶指数降低，会进一步提高纤维的柔顺性；文中将更高的分子链运动性、可及性和WRV作为相关因素提及。 [3]
软木浆在PFI中纤维长度下降、细小纤维含量上升；硬木浆的纤维长度变化不显著，但图1显示其细小纤维含量随PFI增加。 [1]
对湿纸幅强度而言，纤维长度起关键作用，因此长纤维的软木浆湿纸幅强度增幅更明显。 [1]
在提供的证据中，没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量比较或排序；湿纸幅强度结果也不足以确定成纸强度贡献排名，因此无法判定哪个因素贡献最大。 [1]

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(30) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1). [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34]. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(30)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(30) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

[原文]
Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

claims.text: PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍连接）、纤维切断变短和细小纤维生成。
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。
由WRV表征的润胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。
PFI提高了片材拉伸强度，而zero-span拉伸指数表明PFI未降低纤维本身强度。
分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少以及结晶指数降低，会进一步提高纤维的柔顺性；文中将更高的分子链运动性、可及性和WRV作为相关因素提及。
软木浆在PFI中纤维长度下降、细小纤维含量上升；硬木浆的纤维长度变化不显著，但图1显示其细小纤维含量随PFI增加。
对湿纸幅强度而言，纤维长度起关键作用，因此长纤维的软木浆湿纸幅强度增幅更明显。
在提供的证据中，没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量比较或排序；湿纸幅强度结果也不足以确定成纸强度贡献排名，因此无法判定哪个因素贡献最大。

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[原文]
Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34]. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds. [章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds [原文] As to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. [原文]
Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

original_draft.answer: PFI打浆的增强路径是：机械作用先造成内/外细纤维化、纤维变短和细小纤维生成[2]；细纤维化增加比表面积与孔隙，使打浆度和WRV上升[1]；纤维吸水润胀后更柔顺，有助于提高纤维间结合强度，而zero-span拉伸指数显示单纤维强度并未下降[1]。分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少和结晶指数降低，也会提高柔顺性、可及性和WRV[3]。因此成纸变结实与纤维间结合能力提高一致。三因素中，证据没有给出定量贡献排序：若指湿纸幅强度，纤维长度被明确为关键；若指纤维间结合/成纸强度，WRV/润胀是文中明确强调的机制，但不能判定它相对细小纤维或长度贡献最大[1]。

claims.text: PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍连接）、纤维切断变短和细小纤维生成。
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。
由WRV表征的润胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。
PFI提高了片材拉伸强度，而zero-span拉伸指数表明PFI未降低纤维本身强度。
分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少以及结晶指数降低，会进一步提高纤维柔顺性、可及性和WRV。
软木浆在PFI中纤维长度下降、细小纤维含量上升，而硬木浆的这些参数变化不显著。
对湿纸幅强度而言，纤维长度起关键作用，因此长纤维的软木浆湿纸幅强度增幅更明显。
文中没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量比较或排序。

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(30) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.

Abstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.

PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍连接）、纤维切断变短和细小纤维生成。 [2]
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。 [2]
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。 [1]
由WRV表征的润胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。 [1]
PFI提高了片材拉伸强度，而zero-span拉伸指数表明PFI未降低纤维本身强度。 [1]

initial_answer.answer: PFI打浆的增强路径是：机械作用先造成内/外细纤维化、纤维变短和细小纤维生成[2]；细纤维化增加比表面积与孔隙，使打浆度和WRV上升[1]；纤维吸水润胀后更柔顺，有助于提高纤维间结合强度，而zero-span拉伸指数显示单纤维强度并未下降[1]。分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少和结晶指数降低，也会提高柔顺性、可及性和WRV[3]。因此成纸变结实与纤维间结合能力提高一致。三因素中，证据没有给出定量贡献排序：若指湿纸幅强度，纤维长度被明确为关键；若指纤维间结合/成纸强度，WRV/润胀是文中明确强调的机制，但不能判定它相对细小纤维或长度贡献最大[1]。

claims.text: PFI打浆对纤维的主要作用包括内细纤维化（纤维壁分层、松弛和润胀）、外细纤维化（表面微细纤维剥离但仍连接）、纤维切断变短和细小纤维生成。
这些作用会提高纤维的可及性、润胀、柔顺性和纤维间结合能力。
随PFI转数增加，打浆度和WRV显著上升，原因是更高程度的细纤维化产生了新的表面和更多孔隙。
由WRV表征的润胀使纤维在横向更柔顺，有助于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度。
PFI提高了片材拉伸强度，而zero-span拉伸指数表明PFI未降低纤维本身强度。
分子层面上，部分分子间O(6)H···O(3′)氢键减少以及结晶指数降低，会进一步提高纤维柔顺性、可及性和WRV。
软木浆在PFI中纤维长度下降、细小纤维含量上升，而硬木浆的这些参数变化不显著。
对湿纸幅强度而言，纤维长度起关键作用，因此长纤维的软木浆湿纸幅强度增幅更明显。
文中没有给出纤维长度、细小纤维和WRV三者对成纸强度贡献的定量比较或排序。

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively.  On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[原文]
 On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

提供的表格（表1、表2）、方法描述和图3a中没有针叶木8000转组干纸抗张指数每次平行实验的逐次原始数据；图3a在该转数只有一个汇总点及误差棒。 [1] [2] [6] [8]
表1只列出针叶木和阔叶木在不同PFI转数下的结晶指数CI与微晶尺寸，不含干纸抗张指数或平行实验值。 [1]
方法部分仅说明干纸抗张强度按TAPPI T494测试，未报告平行实验次数或逐次测量值。 [6]
图3a以折线和散点给出针叶木干纸抗张指数随PFI转数的变化，每个转数只显示一个汇总点及误差棒，而非每次平行实验的原始数据。 [8]
按图3a红色右轴估读，针叶木8000转处干纸抗张指数的汇总均值约为80 N·m/g，但图中未列出该点对应的多次平行原始值。 [8]

The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining.  On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds

As to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \mathrm { H } \cdots \mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].

In the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.

[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

candidate.answer:
PFI磨浆提高了纤维分丝帚化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且没有降低纤维本身的抗张强度。 [4]
干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI磨浆过程中的分丝帚化和细组分增加。 [4]
Figure 3显示，无论软木还是硬木，干纸抗张指数（红色曲线）都随PFI磨浆转数增加而上升，并在较高转数下趋于平缓。 [2]
方法部分列出的力学测试是干纸抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零距抗张强度，未列出耐破或撕裂测试。 [1]
在提供的图表和摘录中，纤维形态、打浆度/WRV以及抗张、零距抗张和湿纸幅强度均有报告；这些图表和摘录未提供耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数值。 [2] [4] [5]

original_draft.answer: 论文的结论是：PFI磨浆促进分丝帚化和细组分增加，使干纸抗张强度随磨浆转数提高，同时零距抗张所反映的纤维强度没有下降；作者将干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于分丝帚化和细组分增加[4][2]。所给证据中没有耐破指数和撕裂指数的测试或数值，方法部分列出的力学测试为干纸抗张、湿纸幅抗张和零距抗张，因此无法给出这两项的精确数据[1][2][5]。

claims.text: PFI磨浆提高了纤维分丝帚化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且没有降低纤维本身的抗张强度。
干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI磨浆过程中的分丝帚化和细组分增加。
Figure 3显示，无论软木还是硬木，干纸抗张指数（红色曲线）都随PFI磨浆转数增加而上升，并在较高转数下趋于平缓。
方法部分列出的力学测试是干纸抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零距抗张强度，未列出耐破或撕裂测试。
所给结果图表报告的是纤维形态、打浆度/WRV以及抗张、零距抗张和湿纸幅强度，未提供耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数值。

PFI磨浆提高了纤维分丝帚化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且没有降低纤维本身的抗张强度。 [4]
干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI磨浆过程中的分丝帚化和细组分增加。 [4]
Figure 3显示，无论软木还是硬木，干纸抗张指数（红色曲线）都随PFI磨浆转数增加而上升，并在较高转数下趋于平缓。 [2]
方法部分列出的力学测试是干纸抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零距抗张强度，未列出耐破或撕裂测试。 [1]
在提供的图表和摘录中，纤维形态、打浆度/WRV以及抗张、零距抗张和湿纸幅强度均有报告；这些图表和摘录未提供耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数值。 [2] [4] [5]

claims.text: PFI磨浆提高了纤维分丝帚化、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且没有降低纤维本身的抗张强度。
干纸抗张强度的提高主要归因于PFI磨浆过程中的分丝帚化和细组分增加。
Figure 3显示，无论软木还是硬木，干纸抗张指数（红色曲线）都随PFI磨浆转数增加而上升，并在较高转数下趋于平缓。
方法部分列出的力学测试是干纸抗张强度、湿纸幅强度和零距抗张强度，未列出耐破或撕裂测试。
在提供的图表和摘录中，纤维形态、打浆度/WRV以及抗张、零距抗张和湿纸幅强度均有报告；这些图表和摘录未提供耐破指数或撕裂指数的精确数值。

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.2. Morphological Analysis of Fibers and Mechanical Properties of Sheets
[原文]
The fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Mechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
 It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].

There are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
Fourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction
[原文]
There is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions
[原文]
The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.

[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining
[原文]
Commercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.
